author: A Robot
objectives: Students will identify the structural components of DNA.
Students will apply the complementary base-pairing rules.
Students will describe the antiparallel orientation of DNA strands.
Students will trace the action of replication enzymes at the fork.
Students will explain why replication is semiconservative.

modules.description: An introduction to the 3D structure of the DNA double helix.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify the sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.
Apply complementary base-pairing rules A-T and G-C.
instructions: Observe the DNA structure from different angles.

clips.changeMeaning: Introduce the DNA double helix structure, highlighting the sugar-phosphate backbone and the internal nitrogenous base pairings.
clips.narration: DNA, the molecule of life, forms a stable double helix. Notice the two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones spiraling around a common axis.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlight the specific complementary base pairing rules, focusing on hydrogen bonds between Adenine-Thymine and Guanine-Cytosine.
clips.narration: The nitrogenous bases project inward. Adenine pairs with thymine via two hydrogen bonds, while guanine pairs with cytosine via three. This complementary pairing ensures structural stability.

modules.description: Step-by-step walkthrough of semiconservative DNA replication.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Trace the roles of helicase, polymerase, and ligase.
Explain the continuous vs discontinuous synthesis of strands.
Articulate why the process is semiconservative.
instructions: Follow the replication fork as the enzymes operate.

clips.changeMeaning: Show helicase unwinding the double helix and single-strand binding proteins stabilizing the newly exposed DNA templates.
clips.narration: Replication begins as helicase unwinds the double helix, creating a replication fork. Single-strand binding proteins stabilize the exposed strands.

clips.changeMeaning: Show DNA polymerase synthesizing the leading strand continuously and the lagging strand discontinuously as Okazaki fragments.
clips.narration: DNA polymerase synthesizes new DNA in the 5' to 3' direction. The leading strand is synthesized continuously, while the lagging strand is built in discontinuous Okazaki fragments.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlight the final semiconservative products, illustrating how each daughter molecule retains one original strand and one new strand.
clips.narration: Once ligase joins the fragments, we see the result: each daughter molecule is semiconservative, containing one original parental strand and one newly-synthesized strand.
